original_question: Is the union of the closed geodesics always dense in the manifold?
target_in_paper: Question 8.5.1 in the PDF preprint version of the paper (the same item appears as Question 8.4.1 in the arXiv v3 HTML rendering): "Is the union of the closed geodesics always dense in the manifold?" ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's official question almost verbatim and correctly focuses on density in the manifold itself, rather than on existence or counting of closed geodesics. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
missing_details: The ambient setting is a smooth closed manifold M equipped with a smooth Riemannian metric g; without this, the draft is not fully stand-alone and could be misread as applying to noncompact manifolds or to non-Riemannian settings. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))

The quantifier is universal over the metric on the closed manifold under discussion: the question asks whether the density conclusion holds for every such Riemannian metric, not merely for generic metrics. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))

The phrase "union of the closed geodesics" should be made explicit as the subset of M consisting of points lying on at least one closed geodesic; Section 1 supplies the paper's underlying notion of geodesic and closed geodesic. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))

"Dense in the manifold" means dense in M itself, not density of tangent vectors in the unit tangent bundle SM; the latter is a different question asked immediately before this one. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))

No ambient ring/field, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, operator-power, or "for all sufficiently large m" conditions are relevant here; the omitted context is geometric and topological, not algebraic. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
refined_question: Given a smooth closed manifold M with a smooth Riemannian metric g, is the subset of M consisting of all points that lie on at least one closed g-geodesic dense in M? ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
justification: The draft is already extremely close to the exact paper statement. The official target is the stand-alone question in the subsection on density in the manifold, where the surrounding sentence explains that the authors are now asking density questions in M itself and are no longer assuming the metric is generic. This distinguishes your draft from the immediately preceding question about density of tangent vectors to closed geodesics in SM and from the immediately following question about the existence of a single geodesic dense in a compact surface of positive genus. Section 1 provides the paper-wide notation for M, SM, geodesic flow, and closed geodesics, which is the missing context needed to make the question fully stand-alone and paper-faithful. ([aimath.org](https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/geodesicsproblems.pdf))
